Writer and editor

Pick one

I am Senior Associate Director of Content at The Humane League, a global nonprofit working to end factory farming.

As an activist, I know how to move people into action. Through my work, I’ve learned how to distill complex issues for everyday people and build consensus across diverse constituencies by pinpointing the values they hold in common. I develop persuasive messaging to reach everyone from journalists to food executives to major donors. Ultimately, my goal as an advocate is to inspire people to give of their time or their money to influence decision-makers across the food industry, while making sure that our most loyal supporters feel informed, valued, and motivated to deepen their engagement with us over time. My cross-functional team has raised $1+ million annually through digital fundraising campaigns since 2023, in addition to driving 1.6+ million supporter actions since 2022.

State of Slaughter

The Humane League · interactive report · read the report (PDF)

“The State of Slaughter” is an interactive visualization and research report that analyzes a year of US slaughterhouse violations. I owned the research, writing, and editing, and I co-ideated the design.

Drop bibigo

The Humane League · campaign site

“Drop bibigo” is a campaign site asking the athletes and artists who partner with bibigo to drop their sponsorships. Drawing on linocut illustration, I directed the hero image grid, the falling “DROP / BIBIGO” text, the “SAY / BIBINO” wordplay, and the two-tone offset type, and I used Claude to build the site.

THL’s history

The Humane League · interactive timeline

This timeline for The Humane League was built to deepen donor engagement and retention. I owned the narrative architecture, research, writing, editing, and quality assurance. I collaborated with a developer and a designer to build a personalized, interactive experience combining text and video.

As a dramaturg, I’ve played a curatorial and editorial role at acclaimed Off-Broadway and regional theaters: Playwrights Horizons, Page 73, and Yale Repertory Theater.

As an artist, I know how to craft something beautiful and true. I understand how the real-time creative process unfolds on paper, in the rehearsal room, and on the stage. I’m deeply attuned to the elements of good storytelling—style, tone, structure, audience—and to what will and won’t “read” for a crowd. Much of what it means to be a dramaturg is to think and build alongside writers, directors, and actors. You’re part editor, part curator, part therapist, and part doula, and you’re there to make sure the story has what it needs to thrive. To that end, I’ve worked in close collaboration with playwrights on plays, podcasts, essays, and interviews, offering tailored feedback on everything from character design to AP style.

Heroes of the Fourth Turning

Playwrights Horizons · 2020 Pulitzer Prize Finalist

Will Arbery’s play, directed by Danya Taymor, was a 2020 Pulitzer Prize Finalist. As dramaturg, I was a sounding board and second set of eyes for the company and wrote a contextual essay for audiences, “The Trouble with Empathy.”

Almanac

Playwrights Horizons · literary magazine, 2021

I started a new literary magazine for an Off-Broadway theater and served as its inaugural editor-in-chief. I set the vision, wrote for, and edited the first issue.

I hold a Doctor of Fine Arts in Dramaturgy and Dramatic Criticism from the Yale School of Drama (now called the David Geffen School of Drama at Yale).

As a scholar, I know how to go about research, analyze the data, build tight arguments, and then teach what I’ve learned. I can get quickly up to speed on new corpora of knowledge. My doctoral research asked how theater and performance represent ecological science and scale. From the history of science to literary criticism to the rise of industrial agriculture in the US, I’m a confident and curious researcher who can come away from the library or the archives with clear syntheses of the most valuable takeaways.
